blocks.text: Why Slack is the primary tool for technical account managers

As a technical account manager, your value lies in your ability to translate technical data into client solutions. Slack acts as your command center. It holds the history of client issues, internal engineering discussions, and project status updates. On a Mac, the desktop app is more powerful than the browser version because it supports native system notifications and global keyboard shortcuts. You spend most of your day in this app, so every second saved on navigation adds up.
Essential Slack keyboard shortcuts for Mac

You should never touch your mouse to switch channels. Use the Quick Switcher by pressing Command ⌘ + K. Type the first few letters of the client channel name and hit Enter. To search for a specific technical error code or a past conversation, press Command ⌘ + G. If you need to see all your unread messages, use Command ⌘ + Shift + A. These shortcuts are identical to the Windows versions, just swap the Command ⌘ key for the Control key.

items: Command ⌘ + K: Open the Quick Switcher for instant channel navigation.
Command ⌘ + G: Open the search bar to find messages across your workspaces.
Command ⌘ + ,: Open Slack preferences to manage notification sounds and display settings.
Shift + Enter: Create a new line in a message without sending it.
Command ⌘ + /: View the built-in cheat sheet for all available shortcuts.

blocks.text: Advanced search techniques for technical data

Technical account managers often search for specific logs or past engineering decisions. A basic keyword search returns too much noise. Use modifiers to narrow your results. Type from: followed by a colleague's name to find their specific status updates. Use in: followed by a channel name to restrict your search to a specific client project. Combine these with has:link or has:file to find technical documentation or shared reports. This is the fastest way to retrieve information during a client call.

The constant flow of notifications is the biggest enemy of a technical account manager. If you are working on a complex technical report, pause your notifications. Click your profile picture in the bottom left, select Pause notifications, and choose a duration. You can also use the /dnd command followed by a time duration directly in the message box. This signals to your team that you are currently in deep work mode.

If Slack starts feeling sluggish, clear the cache. Go to the Help menu, select Troubleshooting, and then choose Clear Cache and Restart. This often resolves performance issues after long sessions of heavy file sharing.

blocks.text: How Lazur helps you in Slack

Lazur is a voice assistant that lives in your Mac notch. It sees your screen when you hold the shortcut. If you are stuck in a complex Slack menu, hold Option ⌘ and ask Lazur where a specific setting is located. It will draw a circle around the button for you. If you need to draft a technical summary, hold the fn key to dictate your thoughts. Lazur ensures your text is formatted correctly at the cursor, saving you from manual typing errors.

faq.question: Can Lazur click buttons in Slack for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not click buttons or operate apps for you. It points at the screen or guides you through steps so you can perform the actions yourself.

faq.question: What is the fastest way to jump to a specific channel?
faq.answer: Press Command ⌘ + K to open the Quick Switcher, type the channel name, and press Enter.

faq.question: Does Lazur save my Slack messages?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only processes audio and screenshots while you hold the shortcut. It does not store your content or use it to train AI models.

faq.question: How do I see all keyboard shortcuts in Slack?
faq.answer: Press Command ⌘ + / inside the Slack desktop app to open the full list of available shortcuts.
